about: Guidance lines for Hum & Bell sessions. Plain, secular instructions; no claims about health or outcomes. Sessions pick lines from these lists with a seeded random number generator, so a shared link replays the same session. Ordered lists (body, kindness) are used in order.

breath.name: Breath
breath.title: Settle with the breath
breath.summary: Rest your attention on the feeling of breathing, and come back to it whenever you notice you've drifted.

counting.name: Counting
counting.title: Count the breath
counting.summary: Count breaths from one to ten, then start again. Losing count is part of it.

body.name: Body scan
body.title: Body scan
body.summary: Move your attention slowly through the body, from the feet to the head, noticing whatever is there.

sound.name: Listening
sound.title: Listening
sound.summary: Let sounds come and go, the session's own and the room's, without naming or judging them.

kindness.name: Kindness
kindness.title: Kindness
kindness.summary: Silently offer simple good wishes: to yourself, someone you love, someone you hardly know, and everyone.

word.name: A word
word.title: Repeat a word
word.summary: Silently repeat a simple word of your choosing, and let it become quieter and slower.

open.name: Open awareness
open.title: Open awareness
open.summary: Rest in whatever is happening, sounds, sensations, thoughts, without holding on to any of it.

gratitude.name: Gratitude
gratitude.title: Gratitude
gratitude.summary: Bring to mind, one at a time, a few things you're glad of today, and stay with each for a while.

silent.name: Silent timer
silent.title: Silent sitting
silent.summary: No voice. Just sound and bells to mark the start, the end, and any intervals you choose.

arrive: Welcome. Find a way of sitting or lying that you can stay with for a while.
Let's begin. Settle into your seat, and let your hands rest wherever they're comfortable.
Take a moment to arrive. There's nowhere else you need to be for the next little while.
Welcome to this session. Let your eyes close, or rest your gaze softly on the floor.
Find a comfortable position. Upright if you can, but not stiff.
Begin by noticing that you're here. Sitting, breathing, listening.
Let your body settle into whatever is supporting it: the chair, the cushion, the floor.
Welcome. Give yourself permission to set everything else aside, just for now.
Let's start by simply stopping. Nothing to do, nothing to fix.
Settle in. If it helps, take one slower breath than usual, and let it go.
Welcome. Let the sound fill the room, and let yourself be still in it.
Find a posture that feels steady and easy at the same time.
Begin by letting your shoulders drop a little, and your jaw loosen.
Welcome back to stillness. Take a moment to notice how you are, right now.
Arrive here, in this place, at this time. That's enough to begin with.
Let your hands rest. Let your face soften. Let's begin.
settle: Notice the places where your body touches what's holding it.
Feel the weight of your body, and let it be held.
Notice the temperature of the air on your skin.
There's no right way to feel. Just notice what's here.
If your mind is busy, that's fine. Let it be busy in the background.
Let your breathing find its own pace. You don't need to control it.
Notice any sounds around you, near and far.
Let go of any effort you don't need.
Feel your feet, or whatever is touching the ground.
Soften around the eyes. Let the forehead be smooth.
If something is pulling at your attention, acknowledge it, and let it wait.
Notice the rise and fall of the body as it breathes.
Let each out-breath be a little letting go.
Let the drone carry you. You don't have to do anything with it.
Allow yourself to be exactly as you are.
Notice where in the body feels easy, and rest there for a moment.
breath: Bring your attention to the breath. Wherever you feel it most clearly.
Notice the breath coming in, and the breath going out.
You might feel it at the nostrils, the chest, or the belly. Choose one place and rest there.
Feel the whole length of an in-breath, from its beginning to its end.
Notice the small pause at the end of each out-breath.
There's no need to breathe in any special way. Just notice the breath as it is.
Each breath is a little different. See if you can notice how.
Let your attention ride the breath, like resting on a gentle wave.
Notice the cool air coming in, and the slightly warmer air going out.
If the breath is shallow, let it be shallow. If it's deep, let it be deep.
Stay with this breath. And now this one.
Feel the belly rise as you breathe in, and fall as you breathe out.
Notice the moment the in-breath turns into the out-breath.
Let the breath breathe itself. You're just keeping it company.
Rest your attention on the breath as lightly as a feather.
Each time you return to the breath, it's a fresh start.
Notice the breath without trying to improve it.
Follow one full breath, in and out, as closely as you can.
breath_late: Keep resting with the breath, gently.
If you've drifted, that's normal. Come back to the next breath.
Let the breath become the background of your attention, steady and easy.
Notice how the breath goes on by itself, moment after moment.
See if you can stay with the breath for just a few breaths at a time.
Rest in the rhythm of breathing.
Let your attention be soft, and the breath be close.
Nothing to achieve here. Just breathing, and knowing you're breathing.
counting: On the next out-breath, count one. On the next, two. Count up to ten, then begin again at one.
Count each out-breath, quietly in your mind. One. Two. Three.
If you lose count, simply start again at one. That's part of the practice.
If you find you've counted past ten, smile at it, and begin again.
Let the number sit at the end of the breath, like a soft full stop.
Keep counting, one to ten, as slowly as the breath goes.
Each number is a small reminder to be here.
Notice the space between the numbers.
If counting feels effortful, let the numbers become quieter.
One breath, one number. Nothing more.
There's no prize for reaching ten. Starting again is just as good.
Keep the count light, and the breath easy.
counting_late: Keep counting gently. Back to one whenever you lose your place.
If you like, let the counting fall away, and simply rest with the breath.
Count, or just breathe. Either is fine now.
Notice how often the mind wanders, and how often it comes back.
Let the numbers become slower, and softer.
body: Bring your attention down to your feet. Notice whatever sensations are there.
Notice the soles of the feet, the toes, the tops of the feet.
Move your attention up to your ankles and lower legs.
Notice your knees, and the backs of the knees.
Bring your attention to your thighs, and the weight of your legs.
Notice your hips, and where you meet the seat beneath you.
Bring your attention to your lower back. Notice it without trying to change it.
Notice your belly, rising and falling with each breath.
Move up to your chest. Feel it widen a little with each in-breath.
Notice your upper back and shoulder blades.
Bring your attention to your hands. The palms, the fingers, the backs of the hands.
Notice your wrists, forearms and elbows.
Move up through the upper arms to the shoulders. Let them be heavy.
Notice your neck, front and back.
Bring your attention to your jaw. Let it soften.
Notice your mouth, your lips, your tongue resting in the mouth.
Notice your nose, and the breath moving through it.
Bring your attention to your eyes and the small muscles around them.
Notice your forehead and temples.
Move your attention to the top of your head.
Now widen your attention to include the whole body at once.
Feel the whole body sitting here, breathing.
body_late: Rest with the sense of the whole body, from head to feet.
If any area calls for attention, visit it, then widen out again.
Notice the body as a field of changing sensations.
sound: Turn your attention to sound. Let sounds come to you; there's nothing to look for.
Notice the drone. Its low notes and its high notes.
Notice sounds in the room, and sounds beyond the room.
Let each sound arrive and fade, without following it.
Notice how sounds begin, and how they end.
If you find yourself naming a sound, let the name go, and just hear it.
Notice the quietest sound you can hear.
Notice the space in which sounds appear.
Let the sound move through you, like air through an open window.
Some sounds are pleasant, some aren't. Let them all be just sound.
Notice the texture of the sound: smooth, rough, steady, changing.
Listen as if you'd never heard these sounds before.
Notice the sound of your own breathing, among all the others.
sound_late: Let the sounds come and go on their own.
Notice the silence between and beneath the sounds.
Rest your attention in the whole field of sound.
If thoughts come, let them be one more sound, passing.
kindness: Bring to mind yourself, as you are right now. Silently offer yourself these words: may I be safe.
May I be content. May I be at ease.
Let the words be sincere, even if they feel strange. Repeat them slowly: may I be safe, may I be content, may I be at ease.
Now bring to mind someone you love, or someone who has been kind to you. Picture them, or just think of them.
Offer them the same wishes. May you be safe. May you be content. May you be at ease.
Stay with them for a few breaths, repeating the words at your own pace.
Now bring to mind someone you hardly know: someone you passed today, or see now and then.
Offer them the same good wishes, as you would to a friend: may you be safe, may you be content, may you be at ease.
They have a whole life, like yours. Wish them well.
Now widen the circle, to everyone in this building, this street, this town.
May everyone be safe. May everyone be content. May everyone be at ease.
Let the circle grow to include all people, everywhere.
May all beings be safe. May all beings be content. May all beings be at ease.
kindness_late: Keep repeating the words gently, for whoever comes to mind.
If the words feel empty, that's fine. The intention is enough.
Let the wishes settle, like a warm light, wherever you send them.
Rest for a while in simply wishing well.
Come back to the words whenever you notice you've drifted.
word: Choose a simple word to repeat silently. One, or calm, or here. Whatever feels easy.
Begin to repeat your word silently, without moving your lips.
Let the word come easily, in its own time. There's no rhythm to keep.
If thoughts come, notice them, and gently return to your word.
Let the word become softer, as if it were further away.
There's no need to concentrate hard. Let the word be light.
If the word changes or fades, that's fine. Come back to it when you notice.
Let the word and the breath find each other, or not. Either is fine.
Repeat the word as if you were listening to it, rather than saying it.
Let the gaps between the words grow longer if they want to.
Each time you return to the word, return easily.
The word is just a place to rest.
word_late: Keep returning to your word, lightly.
Let the word become quieter still.
If the word has fallen away and you're simply resting, rest.
Notice the quiet around the word.
open: Let your attention open. Nothing to focus on, nothing to keep out.
Notice whatever is most noticeable right now: a sound, a sensation, a thought.
Let experiences come and go, like weather passing through the sky.
If you notice thinking, you can silently note: thinking. Then let it go.
If you notice a sound, note: hearing. If a sensation: feeling.
Rest as the one who notices, rather than the things noticed.
Let your attention be wide, like a quiet room with the windows open.
Notice how everything changes, moment to moment.
There's no need to follow anything. Let it all pass through.
Notice when the mind settles, and when it stirs.
If you get caught up in something, notice that too, and open again.
Rest in the simple fact of being aware.
Let the drone, the breath, the body and the thoughts all be here together.
Nothing to hold. Nothing to push away.
open_late: Let whatever arises, arise. Let whatever passes, pass.
Notice the stillness that's here alongside the movement.
If you've narrowed in on something, gently widen again.
gratitude: Bring to mind one thing you're glad of today. It can be very small.
Stay with it for a few breaths. Notice how it feels to remember it.
Now bring to mind someone you're grateful for. Picture their face.
Notice what it is about them you appreciate.
Bring to mind something your body did for you today.
Think of a place you love, and let yourself be there for a moment.
Bring to mind a moment from this week that went well.
Notice something in this room you're glad to have.
Think of a meal, a conversation, or a walk you enjoyed recently.
Bring to mind someone who helped you without being asked.
Notice the simple fact of being able to sit here and breathe.
Let one more thing you're grateful for come to mind on its own.
Rest with whatever feeling is here, without needing to name it.
If nothing comes to mind, that's fine. Rest with the breath, and see what arrives.
gratitude_late: Let the sense of gratitude settle, and rest in it.
If another thing you're glad of comes to mind, welcome it.
Rest in the breath, with a little warmth around it.
Let the feeling be as big or as small as it is.
wander: If your mind has wandered, that's what minds do. Notice where it went, and come back.
Noticing that you've drifted is a moment of waking up. Gently return.
If you're lost in thought, there's no need to be hard on yourself. Simply begin again.
Wherever your attention is now, see if you can bring it home, kindly.
Thoughts will come. Let them pass like clouds, and come back.
If you're planning or remembering, let that be, and return to the practice.
Each return is the practice. Not staying, but coming back.
If you feel restless, let the restlessness be here too.
If you feel sleepy, you can sit up a little straighter, or open your eyes.
No need to chase the thoughts away. Just stop following them.
Come back, as many times as it takes.
Notice where you are right now. Then return, gently.
If a feeling is strong, let it be here, and stay with the practice alongside it.
However the session is going, it's going fine.
silence: I'll leave you in silence for a while.
Let's continue in silence for a few minutes.
Stay with this in your own way for a while.
I'll be quiet now. The bell will bring you back.
Rest here in silence for a time.
Continue on your own now. There's no rush.
close: In a few moments, the bell will sound. Stay with the practice until then.
Begin to let the practice go, and simply rest.
Notice how you are now. There's no need to judge it.
Let your attention widen to the whole body, sitting here.
Notice the sounds around you, and the room you're in.
Begin to bring a little movement back: fingers, toes, a gentle stretch.
When you're ready, let your eyes open, slowly.
Take a moment before moving on. Notice how this time felt.
Thank yourself for taking this time.
As you go on with your day, see if you can carry a little of this stillness with you.
Let the last sounds fade, and come back gently.
Before you move, take one easy breath.
Whatever happened in this session, you showed up for it.
Let's close here. Return to the room, in your own time.
interval: Halfway. Gently come back to the practice.
A reminder to return, if you've drifted.
Notice where your attention is. Then begin again.
